title: Demo calibration set: openly licensed photos of electrical work
note: A demo set of 7 openly licensed Wikimedia Commons photos, not the study set: the pre-registered study runs on the ministry's dummy data.

items.credit: Electrician installing socket 20160817, Santeri Viinamäki, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons (resized, metadata removed)

CON/N0604.PC8.reason: No packed fixtures, trolley or wheelbarrow are visible — only hands and loose cables at the wall box.
No switch or socket plates are installed in the pictured area, so their positions relative to any drawing cannot be confirmed.
There are no plates or fitted coverings visible in the image to assess levelness, flush fit or screw tightness.

CON/N0605.PC6.reason: Photo shows stripped conductors of varying lengths but does not show the socket terminal depth or final insertion to confirm correct length.
Wires are visible and some are held near the terminals, but the photo does not show them actually placed or secured in labeled phase/neutral/earth terminals.
No visible insulating tape, sleeving on the exposed terminations, or circuit identification labels on the cables in the photo.

CON/N0602.PC6.reason: Photo shows a wire stripper and stripped conductors but does not provide a close enough view of the copper to confirm presence or absence of nicks.
Several individual bare conductors are visible and not joined into a tight, even twist; no completed twisted splice is shown.
Multiple bare copper ends are exposed in the box and no tape or connector covering the joints is visible.

items.credit: Fuse box hager, Dmitry G, CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons (resized, metadata removed)

CON/N0605.PC2.reason: The photo shows the distribution board internals but not the SLD or full circuit list, so capacity and ways versus the SLD cannot be verified.
MCBs/RCCBs appear mounted in the enclosure, but the single-line diagram and device ratings/positions are not provided, so correspondence cannot be confirmed.
Wire colors and terminations are visible, but actual conductor cross-sections and the required sizes from the drawing/ratings are not shown, so matching cannot be determined.

CON/N0605.PC3.reason: The photo shows the wiring and terminals but does not show any person or action checking for looseness, so the check cannot be confirmed.
Screws are visible and appear seated, but tightness (torque) cannot be verified from the image alone.
Terminals show insulated ferrules and intact insulation with no exposed bare copper or stray strands visible.

CON/N0605.PC7.reason: A green/yellow conductor with a ring lug is bolted to the panel/mounting bracket at the right, showing the panel body bonded to an earth connection.
The photo shows the lug and bolt but does not provide enough detail to confirm the tightness of the connection or whether the contact area is clean, bare metal.
Multiple green/yellow earth conductors are terminated at the earth/neutral terminal strip at the top of the enclosure, indicating connection to an earth bar within the panel.

items.credit: Installing conduit at a power facility in Queens. 10-08-2019 (48882438227), MTA Capital Construction Mega Projects, CC BY 2.0, Wikimedia Commons (resized, metadata removed)

CON/N0604.PC4.reason: The photo shows installed conduit but does not include the referenced drawing or route, so alignment with the drawing cannot be confirmed.
Conduit runs are predominantly straight and horizontal with visible bends and a junction box at the left end.
Conduits are surface-mounted on supports below the slab/wall surface rather than placed inside a chased wall or below a plaster line.
Multiple couplers and formed bends are visible at joint locations and no open gaps are evident in the photographed area.

CON/N0602.PC7.reason: No pipe vise or die set is visible; the image shows installed conduit, not a threading operation.
Couplings and joints are visible and appear aligned but the photo does not show thread condition or confirm couplings are fully screwed on.
Support strut and clamps are visible and appear installed, but the photo cannot show whether the bracket is firmly fixed or if the conduit moves when pushed.

items.credit: Fil de terre et piquet de terre, Cjp24, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons (resized, metadata removed)

CON/N0604.PC11.reason: A clamp securing the conductor to the rod is visible but there is no clearly visible lug under the terminal—no lug can be confirmed.
A continuity test result or testing instrument is not shown; the photo does not show whether the earth wire was checked end-to-end.
The wire is clearly green-and-yellow and reaches the earth rod in the photo, but the image does not show whether it reaches every metal box and socket earth.

items.credit: KVG-Abstellfläche am Alten Postareal an der Werftstraße, Kiel-Gaarden-Ost - 18, DYVER, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons (resized, metadata removed)

CON/N0603.PC4.reason: Photo is taken from a distance and does not show the screw/bolt/clamp details or allow testing that the light/bracket do not move when pushed.
Wires and a cable path are visible but the conduit entry, insulation condition and any scraping are not clearly shown in the image.
The distribution board/outgoing terminals are not visible in the photo, so connection to the correct terminal cannot be seen.

CON/N0603.PC10.reason: Cable runs are visible lying low and across the ground/road rather than shown following an evidently short, elevated safe route.
Cable is not consistently routed on supports or tied at each vertical support — it is draped and anchored intermittently to fence and pole only.
Visible sections of the cable run along the ground and below the lamp pole, clearly well under 2 m above ground level.

items.credit: Terminating wires in the Manhattan tunnels. 10-08-2019 (48882438152), MTA Capital Construction Mega Projects, CC BY 2.0, Wikimedia Commons (resized, metadata removed)

CON/N0603.PC6.reason: Conductors at the terminals show lugs/ferrules fitted with no exposed bare copper visible beyond the terminations.
Most conductors are terminated with crimped ring/spade lugs bolted to the busbar, indicating use of lugs.
Photo shows final terminations but does not show the work sequence or whether a post‑tightening tug check was performed.

CON/N0604.PC9.reason: Image does not show any isolation switch position, lockout or test instrument readout to confirm the supply is off and dead.
Phase conductors (dark insulated cables) are on separate transformer lugs and green insulated conductors are routed to an earth/ground point, visible on the right.
No obvious stray copper strands are visible at the terminations, but the photo cannot confirm whether screws are properly tightened.

items.credit: South Asian switchboard, Muzammil, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons (resized, metadata removed)

CON/N0604.PC8.reason: Image shows fixed fixtures on a surface but does not show how the fixtures were carried or whether they were in packaging/trolley.
Photo shows installed switch plates but there is no drawing or reference position visible to confirm they match the drawing.
Plates appear uneven and not fully flush with gaps and at least one screw position looks empty/misaligned, so they are not clearly level, flush and firmly screwed.
